questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'no improvement'.**

The sun hid behind a cloud and it seemed like a light (have been switched) off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The subject of the sentence is 'the sun' and the verb used is 'hid' that is past tense. 'behind' is a preposition and after a preposition, we need a prepositional object so 'a cloud' is a prepositional object.
 
• 'and' is coordinate conjunction that is going to take a parallelism rule. hence, 'seemed' is correct. The first action in this clause 'switching off the light' hence this action is going to be written in the past perfect tense.

**So the correct sentence is-** *The sun hid behind a cloud and it seemed like a light **had been switched off.***

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

He said to me, “I go for a walk daily.”

options.text: He told me that he went for a walk daily.
He told me that he goes for a walk daily.
He told me that he daily went for a walk.
He told me that he had gone for a walk daily.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He told me that he goes for a walk daily.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is the direct speech that refers to the daily action hence, from this we can comprehend that the tense of the sentence will not change.
 
• whereas 'said to' will change into 'told' but the tense in the reported speech will not change because the time reference is given that denotes habitual action.
 
• *So the correct indirect speech is-* He told me that he goes for a walk daily.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Corruption not only generates black money but also ______ criminals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'breeds'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **According to grammar,** 'not only...but also is a correlative conjunction hence if after 'not only' the verb is written then after 'but also' verb should be there in the same form.
 
• In the given sentence, *'not only has a verb 'generates' hence 'but also' should also have a verb.* 
 
 
• Let's find out the meaning of the following words:- 
 
• **creeps:** moves slowly and carefully in order to avoid being heard or noticed.
 
• **breeds:-** rears and trains someone to behave in a particular way. 
 
• **deeds: - **an action that is performed intentionally or consciously.
 
 
 
• Clearly, with reference to context, corruption trains criminals to commit more crimes. Hence, **option 2 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She will surely pass if she ______ harder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'studies'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to grammar, whenever the main clause is in the future tense especially in the conditional sentence the subordinate (if-clause) should be in the present tense. Hence, the verb in the blank should be 'studies'

**So the correct sentence is-** *She will surely pass if she **studies** harder.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The injustice from the sentence pronounced (1)/ above that great scientist, is (2)/ now evident to us all. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'2' i.e. error lies in this part of the sentence**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In part 2 of the sentence, the usage of **'above'** is incorrect Instead, use **'on'**

 
• Pronounced on/upon is a phrasal verb that means 'to give your opinion on something, especially in a formal way'
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• It is too early to **pronounce on** the success or failure of the reforestation project. 
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The injustice from the sentence** pronounced on** that great scientist, is now evident to us all.*
